clue.text: In middle of round sheltered by tree

indicators.note: something sheltered by another is held inside it, so the tree wraps round the picked letter

parts.note: the poplar is a tall, fast-growing tree

indicators.note: points to the central letter of the word round

explanation.surface: Someone stands under a tree in the middle of a round of golf, keeping out of the rain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link word but is the definition: what is in fashion is liked by many.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal synonyms for fashionable and widely liked, as in 'the in place to eat'.

clue.text: Study for a purpose

parts.note: per means for each or for a, as in 'ten pounds per head'
use is a purpose or function

explanation.surface: Someone is studying with a specific aim in mind.
explanation.definitionFit: To peruse is to read or examine carefully, which is to study it.

clue.text: Marvel! Right away is able to have sex

indicators.note: the letter for right is sent off from the word

parts.note: a portent can be a prodigy or marvel

explanation.surface: An exclamation of amazement that a man is, after all, capable in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Of a man, potent means capable of sexual intercourse, the opposite of impotent.

clue.text: Sign I'm struggling with rents in Herefordshire town

parts.note: Leo is a sign of the zodiac

indicators.note: struggling letters are in disorder, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tenant of a given star sign is struggling with high rents in a provincial town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggling' rearranges I'M and RENTS into MINSTER. Herefordshire is an English county on the Welsh border.
explanation.definitionFit: Leominster is a market town in the English county of Herefordshire.

clue.text: Winchester's one awfully common pupil gets detention

indicators.note: a pupil in detention is kept in, so the letter is held inside

parts.note: rife means widespread, especially of something bad
L is a learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: At Winchester, a public school, a pupil with vulgar manners is kept in after class.
explanation.walkthrough: Winchester looks like the school but is the rifle maker; Winchester College is a famous English private school.
explanation.definitionFit: The Winchester is a famous make of repeating firearm, so one is an example of this weapon.

clue.text: Refers to big men, both losing their heads

indicators.note: each of the two synonyms drops its first letter, its head

parts.note: a big person is tall
dudes is slang for men or guys

explanation.surface: Someone mentions large men who have both been beheaded, a grisly historical aside.
explanation.definitionFit: To allude is to mention or refer to something indirectly.

clue.text: Liberal hit back: "It's unfair!"

indicators.note: liberal means free and loose, so the letters are rearranged freely

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician retaliates against a rival, complaining of injustice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberal' looks like a politician but signals the anagram of HIT BACK and IT; 's (is) links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is a bit thick is a British idiom calling it unreasonable or unjust.

clue.text: Villa centre half welcomes tie

indicators.note: the word pair takes the letters in, each word giving a half of them

explanation.surface: Aston Villa's centre-half takes on a tied match.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters straddle vilLA CEntre. Aston Villa is an English football club; a centre-half is a central defender.
explanation.definitionFit: To lace shoes is to tie them, using a lace.

clue.text: Full of energy, play with new guide

indicators.note: the play is filled with the energy word

parts.note: a drama is a play
go means energy or vigour

explanation.surface: An energetic new production with a guide to the action.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragoman is an interpreter and guide, historically in Arabic-, Turkish- or Persian-speaking countries.

clue.text: 13 from TV castle — hard

parts.note: a television set
a fort is a fortified building, like a castle
H is hard, as in pencil grades

explanation.surface: Instructions for leaving a TV castle set, hard going.
explanation.walkthrough: '13' points to the answer at 13-down, whose meaning, to set off on a journey, is shared.
explanation.definitionFit: To set forth is to start a journey, just as to hit the road is to depart.

clue.text: Reviewed, in short, erotica from yesteryear

indicators.note: viewed again in reverse, so the hidden letters are read backwards
the letters sit inside the words short and erotica, spanning the gap between them

explanation.surface: A critic has written a brief review of some vintage erotic fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in short' looks like 'briefly', but 'in' signals hidden letters: shORT ERotica holds ORTER, which 'Reviewed' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Retro styles imitate or revive fashions of the past, so the word describes things from yesteryear.

clue.text: Aid to presentation for Pam

parts.note: a chart is a map, and flipping map back to front gives the name Pam

explanation.surface: A colleague named Pam is getting help to prepare a presentation.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: the answer read as an instruction (turn over a chart, i.e. a MAP) produces the clue word Pam.
explanation.definitionFit: A large pad of paper on an easel, its sheets turned over during a talk, is a standard presentation aid.

clue.text: Thoughts of love dismissed? Fancy one's smitten

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate or reworked, so the remaining letters are rearranged
the letter for love is sent away from the fodder

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, a nought or the letter O

explanation.surface: A lovelorn person, their affection rejected, still fancies the one they are smitten with.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove O from ONE'S SMITTEN to leave NESSMITTEN, which 'Fancy' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Sentiments are views or opinions, a close synonym for thoughts.

clue.text: Number two crosses line — game up!

definitions.note: a game played up, that is mounted on horseback

indicators.note: the first word straddles, and so holds, the second

parts.note: a childish euphemism for excrement

explanation.surface: The runner-up has crossed the finish line, and the game is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number two' is a nursery word for excrement, not the second-placed player. 'up' here means riding a horse, as a jockey is 'up'.
explanation.definitionFit: Polo is the team sport played on horseback, so it is a game in which players are mounted.

clue.text: Go to this place saving time, then do a flit

indicators.note: saving means keeping safe within, so the abbreviation is held inside

parts.note: hither means here, to this place

indicators.note: to flit is to move about, so the two words move into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is told to come here quickly and then skip out, a 'do a flit' being British slang for leaving in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'do a flit' reads as one British idiom for absconding, but 'flit' is the anagram signal turning DO A into OAD.
explanation.definitionFit: To hit the road is an idiom for setting off or leaving, so it means to go.

clue.text: "Exciting nights are fiction" (Mrs Vlad?)

indicators.note: to excite is to stir up, so these letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A complaint that thrilling nights exist only in novels, with a cheeky aside about the setter's wife.
explanation.walkthrough: Vlad is the setter; his wife is, by way of example, his partner, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a spouse or long-term partner, and Mrs Vlad would be the setter's wife, an example.

clue.text: Decorate country house for the King

parts.note: to grace is to adorn or decorate
a land is a country or nation

explanation.surface: Someone decorates a country house fit for royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the King' is Elvis Presley, the King of rock and roll, not a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Graceland was Elvis Presley's mansion in Memphis, and he was known as the King.

clue.text: Dominating male Henry caught unawares

indicators.note: the pieces are caught inside the phrase for dominating

parts.note: on top means in control, dominating
he is the male pronoun
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A domineering man called Henry is caught by surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Caught on the hop is a British idiom for caught unprepared or by surprise.

clue.text: Mike supporting Bill Edmondson and Don?

indicators.note: in a down entry a supporting piece goes underneath, so it comes after

parts.note: AC is an account, a bill
Ade Edmondson is a British comedian, star of The Young Ones
mic is short for microphone, also spelt mike

explanation.surface: A list of comedians: Mike backing up Bill, Edmondson and Don.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface lists Comic Strip names; in fact Edmondson gives ADE. 'Don' is a university teacher, with a question mark for the example.
explanation.definitionFit: A don is a lecturer at Oxford or Cambridge, an example of a university scholar.

clue.text: Race, methinks, largely fixed — it won't interest many

indicators.note: a fixed race is rigged; here the letters are rigged into a new order
most of the word, so its last letter is lost

explanation.surface: A punter suspects the race is mostly rigged, though few people will care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'largely' leaves METHINK; with RACE that is rearranged by 'fixed'.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche market is a small specialised segment of buyers, appealing to few customers.

clue.text: Book a top fighter

definitions.meaning: a book of the Old Testament
Anthony ..., the British heavyweight boxing champion

explanation.surface: A boxer being booked for a bout.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to a book of the Bible and to the world heavyweight boxer Anthony Joshua.

clue.text: Yes, Vice-Admiral's first to go above

indicators.note: in a down entry, going above means placed before
only the opening letter of the naval rank is taken

parts.note: greed is one of the seven deadly sins, a vice

explanation.surface: A vice-admiral assents, being first to climb up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vice-Admiral' looks like one rank but splits into Vice and Admiral.
explanation.definitionFit: Agreed! is an exclamation of assent, used just like yes.

clue.text: Keep secret Mr Nasty told

indicators.note: what is told is spoken, so the name is heard rather than seen

parts.note: Mr Hyde is the evil alter ego of Dr Jekyll in Stevenson's story

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to conceal what a villain has confided to them.
explanation.definitionFit: To conceal something or keep it out of view is a standard synonym for keeping it secret.

clue.text: Soon feel at home because of English on board

indicators.note: taken aboard, so held inside the other word

parts.note: to belong somewhere is to feel at ease there
for can mean because of, as in 'jumped for joy'

explanation.surface: A newcomer to a company board will soon feel at ease because they are English.
explanation.definitionFit: Before long means in a short while, an idiomatic synonym for soon.

clue.text: See 14
Possibly saw money being picked up

indicators.note: lifted upwards, which in a down entry reads the word bottom to top

parts.note: loot is slang for money

explanation.surface: Perhaps someone noticed cash being collected from the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saw' looks like a verb (noticed) but is the noun, a cutting implement.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is one example of a hand implement, hence 'Possibly'.

clue.text: In no way a quack, some might say

parts.note: at home means in, as in 'is anyone in?'
O is nought, nothing
a path is a way or track

explanation.surface: Defending a practitioner: they are certainly not a charlatan, though some might claim otherwise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In no way' reads as a single phrase meaning 'not at all', but splits into In, no and way. Sceptics regard homeopathy as quackery, hence 'some might say'.
explanation.definitionFit: Critics consider practitioners of this alternative medicine to be charlatans, so the definition is an opinion rather than a synonym.

clue.text: About to engage with comic hero — it'll provide colour

indicators.note: one piece engages the other by being taken inside it
comic means funny or absurd, so the letters of hero are jumbled

parts.note: C stands for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A comic-book hero is about to clash with a rival, adding colour to the story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comic' rearranges HERO to OHRE, and C goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is an earthy yellow-brown pigment used to make paints, so it supplies colour.

clue.text: Preference was first to get drunk

parts.note: one's pick is one's choice or preference
led means was in front, ahead of the rest

explanation.surface: Whoever was chosen first got drunk, a party-game rule perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Pickled is informal slang for intoxicated, preserved in alcohol.

clue.text: Course director dismissed sign

parts.note: Redcar is a racecourse in North Yorkshire, England

explanation.surface: The director of a racecourse has been fired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Course' is not a path or a meal: it is Redcar, a horse-racing course on the Yorkshire coast.
explanation.definitionFit: In football a referee shows a player this card to signal they are sent off the field.
